answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a real glaciological monitoring post: a sensor bolted into a glacier below a surveyed knoll, maintained by one field operator who reports live readings on unpredictable check-ins. One person cannot staff two ice posts at once, and the permit fee in outside money doubles per post on the same funding trail, so each extra fake identity costs another glacier post, another season of cold-weather labor, and twice the prior fee.
